title: Private Berlin Tour for Groups - FAQ
subtitle: Straight answers for choosing a private or public Berlin walking format.

items.q: When is a private Berlin tour better for a group?
items.a: Choose private when the group wants the walk to itself, needs a date the public calendar does not offer, or needs a pace or theme that a mixed group cannot follow. Share the real priorities before booking so the central route can be assessed honestly.

items.q: Is a free Berlin walking tour enough for a first visit?
items.a: Often, yes. A public walk is a good fit when the group wants a central introduction, can meet at the advertised time and is happy to follow the fixed route. BerlinWalk lasts about 2 hours from the World Clock on Alexanderplatz towards Hackescher Markt; check the live calendar for the date.

items.q: Can I choose which stops the private walk keeps?
items.a: You can ask for a different emphasis inside the central route. I can give the museum row more time, keep the walk shorter and more visual for children, or plan a slower version with real sitting points. The final route and meeting point are confirmed after you share the group details.

items.q: Can a private Berlin tour start somewhere other than Alexanderplatz?
items.a: That is one of the useful reasons to ask about a private format. Share the group size, date, preferred start, must-see places and any pace or access needs through the enquiry form so the route can be assessed before booking.

items.q: How do I choose between a private tour and BerlinWalk's free tour?
items.a: Choose the free tour when a fixed central introduction solves the main problem and the group is happy to walk with strangers. Choose private when you want your own date, only your group, and a central route whose pace and emphasis can be confirmed around your priorities.
